  built by 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action as closed words, ids and counts alone) gains the TEXT of what the step
  caused, per record, from every source:
  - a **panic**: its payload and its source location (file, line, column), as the panic hook already reads them
    (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs`);
  - an **error** the app's root error boundary took: its message AND its cause chain (each `source()` in turn), not
    its top line alone — today `RootErrorMark` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`) holds the error by
    identity and reads nothing of it;
  - a **log record** from the app, the UI framework and the engine: its message, its target (which source said it),
    its level, the location a bridged `log` record carries (`log.file` · `log.line`) and its fields — today the
    capture (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs`) counts records by level alone and admits no engine or escher
    target.

- **The scrub** — every field of every record passes the scrub by field name that already stands on the log sink
  (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`: the content field names, the engine's safe-field rule); a field the
  scrub hides is shown hidden (its name and the redaction marker), and the rest of the message still crosses — a
  message is never blanked because one field in it is. The ratified mask is unmoved: a password's or a file input's
  value never crosses.

- **The bounds, set by measurement** — each message cut at a fixed length; an answer carries at most a fixed count
  of records; both numbers are set from the lengths research measures, so that the usual message arrives whole.
  A cut is never silent: a cut message says it was cut and by how much; the records past the count are counted, by
  source.

- **Every carrier** — the text rides `caused` wherever `caused` rides today: the in-process `Outcome`, the command
  line's JSON line, the session socket's `call`, an MCP tool result and a kept check (recorded, replayed, its answer
  kept whole); the MCP result bound (1,048,576 bytes) and the socket answer bound hold over it.

- **The help** — `describe()`'s self-description names the new fields of `caused` and the cut's and the count's
  meanings.

# The founder's answer on «Error text in the answer» — 2026-11-16

The founder answered one question by question dialog in the overseer session on 2026-11-16; the answer was read at
15:47Z. It is his own chosen label, verbatim; the overseer relays it.

## What of an error's text crosses onto an answer's `caused`

> «Скраб и граница (Recommended)»

The option as it was read to him: the message of every record from every source — the app, the framework and the
engine; every field passes the same scrub by field name that already stands on the log sink (the values of fields
such as a password or a token are hidden); each message is cut at a fixed length; an answer carries a fixed count of
records and the rest are only counted. Its stated price: a long error arrives cut, and the value of a field with a
secret name is not shown to the agent even where a diagnosis would want it. The ratified crossing (a password's and a
file input's value do not cross the socket) stays as it is.

Passed over, as they were read to him:
- the whole text, unscrubbed — every field value as written, a boundary widening by his word, the route entry's
  «scrub held» lifted and the security masters rewritten;
- the scrub kept with no cut — messages uncut and the count of records per answer unbounded.

## The purpose he set for it, typed by him right after the answer, verbatim

> «Надо так чтоб агент понял ошибку и смог разобраться в проблеме, мы строим хедлесс харнесс для него»

The overseer's reading, read back to him in the overseer session and confirmed by him, typed, verbatim: «Все верно» —
how the chosen option is built to that purpose:
- the bound is sized by measurement, not picked: the phase reads the lengths of real messages (a panic with its
  location, an error with its source chain, the engine's and the framework's records on the stand) and sets the cut
  so that the usual message arrives whole;
- a cut is never silent: a cut message says it was cut and by how much, and the records past the count are counted
  by source;
- what an agent needs to find the problem rides with the text: where it happened (the source location a panic or a
  record carries), which source said it, and the error's cause chain, not its top line alone;
- the scrub hides a value by its field's name and nothing else: a message is not blanked because one field in it is;
- the chunk's acceptance asks the question he asks — can an agent, from the answer alone, say what failed and where —
  on a fixture with a real failure, not only that the fields are present.

This confirms the reading of his typed words of the morning (`morning-answers-founder-2026-11-16.md`, item 2): the
text of every source, scrubbed and bounded.

data.head: ## The measurement (before the bound is set)

body:
A temporary probe target `tests/blitz-tests/tests/zz_probe_error_text.rs` (its source kept at
`{work_dir}/evidence/zz_probe_error_text.rs.txt`, removed from the tree after the reading) drove every
actionable control of the four lean tasks, Cells' first three cells (click, `=sum(A0:A3)`, Enter) and the load
page through the harness, and a real-failure fixture, under a recorder subscriber that kept every event's target,
level, message and fields, a chaining panic hook that kept each payload and location, and reads of the root
boundary's and of every registered boundary's error. 39 steps. Two builds:
`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --features dioxus-native-dom/tracing --test zz_probe_error_text -- --nocapture`
(the engine's `tracing` on, as the workspace build compiles it; log `{work_dir}/evidence/probe-tracing.log`) and the
same without the feature (the package-alone build; `{work_dir}/evidence/probe-package.log`). Summarised by
`summarize_probe.py` (scratchpad) over each log.
**Records by source and level, message bytes (min · p50 · p95 · max), engine `tracing` on:**
| source (target crate) | level | count | message bytes |
| engine `blitz_dom::document` | INFO | 20 | 26 · 26 · 26 · 26 — `Focussed node NodeId(21v1)`, one per focus move |
| engine `dioxus_native_dom::mutation_writer` | DEBUG | 104 | 17 · 74 · 83 · 95 — attribute writes holding the attribute's VALUE as typed (`name:value, value:Some("ab12")`) and `NodeId` text |
| framework `dioxus_core` | TRACE | 614 | 17 · 19 · 523 · 4106 — the 4106 a `Debug` dump; a `self` field up to 819 B |
| framework `dioxus_signals` | TRACE | 257 | 82 · 107 · 124 · 124 |
| framework `warnings` | TRACE | 403 | 133 each |
| app (the fixture's handler) | WARN | 1 | 40 — `booking rejected: 4 seats over the limit`, fields `seats` (1 B) and `password` (7 B) |

Package-alone build: the two engine rows are absent (0 records); the framework rows read the same; the app row the
same. **At `warn` and above, no stand step caused any record under either build** — the only warn-or-above record
of the 39 steps is the fixture's own. Records per step: max 253 at every level (Crud typing), at `info` and above
max 2.

**Panics (fixture, both builds):** `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 3` — payload 52 B, location
`tests/blitz-tests/tests/zz_probe_error_text.rs:306:22` (53 B); `called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value:
ParseIntError { kind: InvalidDigit }` — payload 81 B, the location the caller's line (std's `#[track_caller]`).
A location inside a registry dependency is an absolute host path (read on the recorder's metadata: every
`dioxus_core` record's file is `/home/…/.cargo/registry/src/…/dioxus-core-0.7.10/src/runtime.rs`).

**Errors with a cause chain (fixture, both builds):** a handler `Err` built from a three-link chain
(`LoadError` → `SettingsError` → `ParseIntError`): top line 31 B, `{:#}` form 97 B, the chain 3 links / 93 B, read by
`CapturedError`'s `Deref` to `anyhow::Error` and its `chain()` — no new dependency.

**The bound the measurement supports:** the longest message of an admitted class (an app record at any level, a
framework or engine record at `warn` and above, a panic, a boundary error's link) read 97 B, and at most 2 such
records crossed a step. A per-text cut of 1024 bytes holds the longest measured ten times over; a count of 16
records per answer holds the largest measured step eight times over.

An acting answer's `caused` stops being closed words and counts alone. It carries, per record, the text an agent
needs to say what failed and where, and to go after it (the founder's purpose, inputs#I1). Each item says:
- a panic's payload and location;
- an error's message and its whole cause chain, and which boundary took it (the root one or one of the app's own);
- a log record's message, its source, target, level, location and fields.

It does this for every source: the app at every level, and the UI framework and the engine at `warn` and above. Every
field passes the log sink's own scrub by field name. Each text is cut at a fixed length that says how much it cut. An
answer holds a fixed count of items, and the rest are counted by kind and source (inputs#I1: «Скраб и граница
(Recommended)» and its five confirmed points).
The bounds are set from the P3 measurement (`doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` §The measurement):
- **Cut:** 1024 bytes per text. The longest admitted message measured was 97 B.
- **Count:** 16 items per answer. At most 2 admitted records crossed a step.

The text rides every carrier `caused` already rides (arch · contract/acting-verb-results/caused,
security · decision/caused-answer-crossing). It reaches no log line or span field (security ·
decision/no-screen-content-in-logs, arch · contract/command-span/never-fielded). It adds no verb, carrier, exit,
refusal cause, session error, socket or listener.

Every error boundary becomes readable. The document provides dioxus-core's own boundary factory at its root scope
before the first build, so every boundary registers its `ErrorContext` there: the root one and each of the app's own.
P3 measured both. A panic's location comes from a chaining panic hook that escher-telemetry's capture installs once
per process. It is inert unless a capture is open on the panicking thread (the operator's answer at P4, below).

2. **Every boundary readable** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `lib.rs`.
   - **The factory.** An ungated `BoundaryRegistry` (an `Rc<RefCell<Vec<ErrorContext>>>`) and a plain `fn` factory
     that makes an `ErrorContext::new(None)` and registers it in the registry it consumes from context.
   - **Where it is provided.** `DioxusDocument::new` provides both at `ScopeId::ROOT` through `vdom.in_scope`,
     before the first build, as P3 measured.
   - **The marks.** `DioxusDocument::boundary_marks()` returns one mark per registered boundary holding an error,
     compared by `Arc::ptr_eq`. `RootErrorMark` stays as it is. Where the root boundary is not among the registered
     ones (a document built after its vdom's first build), the root one is read through `ROOT_ERROR_BOUNDARY` as
     today.
   - **The read.** A mark reads as a `BoundaryError { boundary: Root | Own, message, chain }`: the message is the
     error's top line (`to_string`), the chain each `anyhow` source after it in order. It reads nothing else and logs
     nothing.
   - Unit tests in `boundary.rs`'s module:
     - a root `Err` reads `Root` with its chain;
     - an `Err` under an `ErrorBoundary` of the app's own reads `Own` with its three-link chain, and the root holds
       none;
     - a second step leaves the first error's mark unchanged;
     - with two contexts registered for one own boundary (the root's and the app's, as measured), each error is read
       once.

4. **The written form and the help** — `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`, `schema.rs`, `schema_tests.rs`,
   `explore.rs`.
   - **The writer.** `caused_item` writes the members in step 3's order, each present only where it holds:
     - `cut` only on a cut text;
     - `chain` only on an error;
     - `fields` and `fields_past` only on a log record.
     The acting answers write `caused_past` after `caused`, only when non-empty, as
     `[{"kind","source","count"}]`. The string escaping stands (arch · contract/answer-json/string-escaping), so a
     newline or an ESC byte in a message is written escaped and the line stays one uncoloured line.
   - **The help.** `CAUSED`'s help is rewritten in the program's own fixed text (arch ·
     decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers). It names:
     - each member, the closed `source` and `boundary` words, the cut's meaning, the 16-item count and `caused_past`;
     - the scrub: content-named fields and an engine record's message shown as `[redacted]`;
     - the stated limits: a `log` crate record read only where the process's telemetry bridged it; an app that
       provides its own boundary factory shadows the document's; a location as the compiler wrote it, a dependency's
       an absolute path; a record from the app's own code holds what the app wrote into its message.

     debug records two items.

body:
Enumerated by `git grep -n -A3 -E 'warn!|error!' -- packages/ ':!packages/escher-telemetry' ':!packages/escher-driver'`:
47 hits. 3 are `compile_error!` (accesskit_xplat ×2, dioxus-native's renderer) and 1 is a doc comment
(blitz-vibey-script `document.rs:258`), which leaves **43 sites**. `stylo_taffy` and `debug_timer` hold none.
**Interpolating an attribute value or text — 6 sites in 5 files, each edited:**
| site | interpolates | becomes |
| `blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:1144` | the link's `href` attribute and the document's URL (`Debug`, 205 B measured) | fixed message; fields `href`, `url` |
| `blitz-dom/src/form.rs:156` | the scheme of the form's `action` attribute | fixed message naming the method (a closed enum); field `url` |
| `blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1542` | the iframe's raw `src` attribute | fixed message; field `src` |
| `blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:248` | a text node's data, in a field named `data` the scrub does not hide | field renamed `text` |
| `dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:53` | the asset request (`Debug`: its URL) | fixed message; field `request` |
| `dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:60` | the same | the same |
**Interpolating nothing of a page or of typed input — 37 sites, no change:**
- **The shell's winit-variant `Debug` (6):** blitz-shell `convert_events.rs` ×5, `window.rs:852`.

Node ids may cross (the operator's review). Under escher's own sink nothing changes: an engine target still prints
its safe fields alone and its message `[redacted]`. The moved values land in fields the sink redacts by their names
(`href`, `url`, `src`, `text`, `request`).

**Reached on a fixture (a temporary probe, removed after its reading;
`{work_dir}/evidence/probe-reach-{tracing,package}.log`):**

- **Engine, workspace build.** A click on a block link with `href="http://[::1"` reaches `pointer.rs:1144`: a `WARN`
  at `blitz_dom::events::pointer`, 205 B, the raw `href` and the document URL in its message. An invalid inline style
  value (`color: notacolour`) reaches `node/element.rs:821`: a `WARN` at `blitz_dom::node::element`, its message fixed
  (22 B), its fields `property` and `value`. Neither appears in the package-alone build (the engine's `tracing` off).

- **Framework, both builds.** A component whose render returns `Err` (`"seven".parse()?`) reaches dioxus-core
  `scope_arena.rs:111`: an `ERROR` at `dioxus_core::scope_arena`, 99 B, «Error while rendering component `…`: invalid

- **Fixture trap.** A link left inline has no box for `Harness::click` to aim at, and the click lands elsewhere — the
  testing rule's inline-element trap, met once in this probe.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the unparseable-link warning's `href` and URL moved into fields
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — the unimplemented-scheme warning's scheme moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the unresolvable-iframe warning's `src` moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` — the text-node error's `data` field renamed `text`
- `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs` — the two asset-fetch warnings' request moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` — a documented `pub const TRACING_COMPILED: bool`, whether this build compiled the engine's log sites, so a check asserts the engine case per build
- `format.rs`: no change — the capture reads the sink's existing `CONTENT_FIELDS` and `REDACTED` for every source; the sink's own engine rule (safe fields alone, message hidden) stays the sink's.

- the engine's `warn!|error!` sites over `git grep` of `packages/` (escher's crates excluded): 47 hits · 6 changed · 41 no-change (3 `compile_error!`, 1 doc comment, 37 classified in §The engine's sites).

- An acting answer's `caused` (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`; `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs`,

  - a **panic**: its payload and its source location (file, line, column), as the panic hook already reads them

  - an **error** the app's root error boundary took: its message AND its cause chain (each `source()` in turn), not

  - a **log record** from the app, the UI framework and the engine: its message, its target (which source said it),

    capture (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs`) counts records by level alone and admits no engine or escher

    its message as text, as an app's and the framework's do, every source's content-named fields hidden by name. The
    engine's `warn` and `error` sites are enumerated (43). Each one that interpolates an attribute value or text into

    dioxus-native, a direct edit of the engine code (`doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` §The
    engine's sites). Node ids may cross. The sink's own engine rule is unchanged on its log lines.]

- On a fixture with a **real failure** (a handler that fails the way an app fails — a panic in a real code path, an
  `Err` with a cause chain, a framework or engine record), an agent reading **the answer alone** can say what failed
  and where: the acceptance asserts the message, the source location and the cause chain are in the answer, not only
  that the fields are present. [measured after the operator's P5 review: no stand step causes a framework or engine
  record at `warn` or above (39 steps, both builds), but a fixture reaches one of each. A framework `ERROR` at
  `dioxus_core::scope_arena` comes from a component whose render returns `Err`, under both builds. An engine `WARN`
  at `blitz_dom::events::pointer` comes from a click on a link whose `href` will not parse, under the workspace
  build, where the engine's `tracing` is compiled; under the package-alone build it is absent, and the check states
  which build it read.]

- **Marker:** 2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-16T18:15:25Z
  (re-synthesised after the operator's P5 review)

It does this for every source: the app at every level, and the UI framework and the engine at `warn` and above. Every
message crosses as text, the engine's included. Every source's content-named fields are hidden by name, and nothing
else is (inputs#I1, the operator's P5 review). Each text is cut at a fixed length that says how much it cut. An
answer holds a fixed count of items, and the rest are counted by kind and source (inputs#I1: «Скраб и граница
(Recommended)» and its five confirmed points).

The engine's `warn` and `error` sites were enumerated: 43. The 6 that interpolated an attribute value or text into
their message now carry that value in a named field the scrub hides — a direct edit of blitz-dom and dioxus-native.
Node ids may cross.

- **Cut:** 1024 bytes per text. The longest admitted message measured was 205 B: the engine's unparseable-link
  warning, before its edit.

Every error boundary becomes readable. The document provides dioxus-core's own boundary factory at its root scope
before the first build, so every boundary registers its `ErrorContext` there: the root one and each of the app's own.
P3 measured both. A panic's location comes from a chaining panic hook that escher-telemetry's capture installs once
per process. It is inert unless a capture is open on the panicking thread (the operator's answer at P4).

2. **The engine's interpolating sites carry the value in a hidden field** — a direct edit of the engine code, the
   operator's direction at the P5 review. Each message becomes fixed text naming what failed, and each value moves
   into a field named in `CONTENT_FIELDS`. The sites are research's table, re-read at HEAD before editing:
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` (the unparseable link): the raw `href` into `href`, the document URL
     into `url`;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` (the unimplemented form scheme): the scheme into `url`, the method (a closed
     enum) staying in the message;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` (the unresolvable iframe): the raw `src` into `src`;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` (a text node laid out alone): its `data` field renamed `text`;
   - `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs`, both asset-fetch warnings: the request into `request`.
   The level, target and `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` gating of each site stay as they are. Each change is flagged
   upstreamable (arch · decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable).
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` gains a documented `pub const TRACING_COMPILED: bool = cfg!(feature =
     "tracing")`, so a check asserts the engine case under the build it runs in.

3. **Every boundary readable** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `lib.rs`.
   - **The factory.** An ungated `BoundaryRegistry` (an `Rc<RefCell<Vec<ErrorContext>>>`) and a plain `fn` factory
     that makes an `ErrorContext::new(None)` and registers it in the registry it consumes from context.
   - **Where it is provided.** `DioxusDocument::new` provides both at `ScopeId::ROOT` through `vdom.in_scope`,
     before the first build, as P3 measured.
   - **The marks.** `DioxusDocument::boundary_marks()` returns one mark per registered boundary holding an error,
     compared by `Arc::ptr_eq`. `RootErrorMark` stays as it is. Where the root boundary is not among the registered
     ones (a document built after its vdom's first build), the root one is read through `ROOT_ERROR_BOUNDARY` as
     today.
   - **The read.** A mark reads as a `BoundaryError { boundary: Root | Own, message, chain }`: the message is the
     error's top line (`to_string`), the chain each `anyhow` source after it in order. It reads nothing else and logs
     nothing.
   - Unit tests in `boundary.rs`'s module:
     - a root `Err` reads `Root` with its chain;
     - an `Err` under an `ErrorBoundary` of the app's own reads `Own` with its three-link chain, and the root holds
       none;
     - a second step leaves the first error's mark unchanged;
     - with two contexts registered for one own boundary (the root's and the app's, as measured), each error is read
       once.

5. **The written form and the help** — `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`, `schema.rs`, `schema_tests.rs`,
   `explore.rs`.
   - **The writer.** `caused_item` writes the members in step 4's order, each present only where it holds:
     - `cut` only on a cut text;
     - `chain` only on an error;
     - `fields` and `fields_past` only on a log record.
     The acting answers write `caused_past` after `caused`, only when non-empty, as
     `[{"kind","source","count"}]`. The string escaping stands (arch · contract/answer-json/string-escaping), so a
     newline or an ESC byte in a message is written escaped and the line stays one uncoloured line.
   - **The help.** `CAUSED`'s help is rewritten in the program's own fixed text (arch ·
     decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers). It names:
     - each member, the closed `source` and `boundary` words, the cut's meaning, the 16-item count and `caused_past`;
     - the scrub: content-named fields shown as `[redacted]`, every message crossing;
     - the stated limits: an engine record exists only in a build that compiled the engine's `tracing`; a `log` crate
       record is read only where the process's telemetry bridged it; an app that provides its own boundary factory
       shadows the document's; a location is as the compiler wrote it, a dependency's an absolute path; a message
       holds what its author wrote into it.
   - **The new field.** A `CAUSED_PAST` field spec joins the five acting verbs after `CAUSED`.
   - `schema_tests.rs` and `json.rs`' unit tables move to the new shape, every member written and absent where it
     must be, rows counted.

6. **The standing check follows the new contract** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_errors.rs`.
   - Its items compare against the per-record shape: the log button's two records are two items, the input's two
     debug records two items.
   - Its `holds_no_sentinel` assertions over the answer, the MCP result and the kept check turn into assertions that
     each sentinel IS in `caused`.
   - Its `command`-span case keeps asserting that no sentinel and no `caused` reaches a span field.
   - The root `Err` case reads the error's text in `caused`, `boundary` `root`, beside the boundary's screen
     rendering.
   - Its `//!` doc is restated.

8. **The hook installs once and changes nothing outside a capture** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/capture_panic_hook.rs`
   (new, one behaviour, one `#[test]` so no other test's panic races it; the operator's note at P4). It installs a
   counting hook, opens a capture once, then panics outside any capture:
   - the counting hook runs exactly once for that panic and nothing is captured;
   - a panic inside a capture is captured with its payload and location, and the counting hook runs for it too;
   - a second and a third `capture` install no further hook — the counting hook still runs once per panic, never
     twice.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs` — the founder's question on real failures of every source, every carrier, both modes, both builds
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the field rule callable by the capture
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the unparseable-link warning's `href` and URL moved into fields
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — the unimplemented-scheme warning's scheme moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the unresolvable-iframe warning's `src` moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` — the text-node error's `data` field renamed `text`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` — `TRACING_COMPILED`
- `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs` — the two asset-fetch warnings' request moved into a field

- escher-telemetry's process checks (`telemetry_scrub`, `telemetry_drop`, `telemetry_panic_hook`), which show that
  the sink prints what it printed, the moved engine values now `[redacted]` fields;

- then the pre-push gate, `stand-repeat` (which `stand_act_error_text` joins by its prefix, per package) and the
  coverage leg.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S4). After the steps are green, /implement runs five one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:

- The factory's provision in `DioxusDocument::new` removed: the own-boundary case of `stand_act_error_text` reads
  failed.
- The `href` interpolation restored in `pointer.rs`'s message: the engine case reads failed under the tracing entry.
